[[Providence Park|Multnomah Stadium]] }} {{1965 Athletic Association of Western Universities football standings}} The '''1965 Oregon State Beavers football team''' represented [[Oregon State University]] in the [[Athletic Association of Western Universities]] (AAWU) during the [[1965 NCAA University Division football season]]. In their first season under head coach [[Dee Andros]], the Beavers compiled a 5–5 record (1–3 in AAWU, seventh), and were outscored 162 to 125.{{cite web|title=1965 Oregon State Beavers Schedule and Results|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=SR/College Football|access-date=September 7, 2016 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/oregon-state/1965-schedule.html}} They had only three home games, two on campus at [[Parker Stadium]] in [[Corvallis, Oregon|Corvallis]] and one at [[Multnomah Stadium]] in [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]]. After ten seasons and a recent [[1965 Rose Bowl|Rose Bowl]] appearance, head coach [[Tommy Prothro]] departed for [[1965 UCLA Bruins football team|UCLA]] in January 1965, and forty-year-old Andros was hired in early February.{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=HVZYAAAAIBAJ&sjid=m_cDAAAAIBAJ&pg=7109%2C94505 |newspaper=Spokane Daily Chronicle |location=Washington |title=Dee Andros named Oregon State grid coach |last=Johnson |first=Bob |date=February 1, 1965 |page=15}}{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=o5cRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=AOMDAAAAIBAJ&pg=6817%2C112246|newspaper=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon|title=Andros begins new job as OSU coach|agency=AP, UPI reports|date=February 2, 1965|page=2B}}{{cite news|title=Andros Gets Beaver Job|newspaper=Statesman (Salem, Oregon)|date=February 2, 1965|page=9|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/6574453/andros_gets_beaver_job/}} A [[United States Marine Corps|Marine]] in World War II, he was the head coach at [[Idaho Vandals football|Idaho]] {{nowrap|([[1962 Idaho Vandals football team|1962]]–[[1964 Idaho Vandals football team|1964]]),}} and had played college football as a [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] at [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma]] in the late 1940s under head coach [[Bud Wilkinson]]. Andros led OSU for eleven years, through [[1975 Oregon State Beavers football team|1975]], compiling a {{nowrap|{{winning percentage|51|64|1|record=y}}}} record, {{nowrap|({{winning percentage|30|37|1|record=y}}}} in AAWU/Pac-8), then was the athletic director until 1985. The Beavers defeated rival [[1965 Oregon Ducks football team|Oregon]] for a second consecutive year, this time on the road in the final installment of the [[Oregon–Oregon State football rivalry|Civil War]] contested at [[Hayward Field]]; when the Beavers returned to Eugene [[1967 Oregon State Beavers football team|two years later]], the Ducks had moved into [[Autzen Stadium]].{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=xf9VAAAAIBAJ&sjid=HuMDAAAAIBAJ&pg=4926%2C4237113 |work=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |last=Uhrhammer |first=Jerry |title=Oregon State wins the
